rows.label: Confidentiality
rows.value: Information accessible only to authorised parties. Violated by: data theft, eavesdropping, credential compromise, unauthorised access. Ask: 'Who can see this who shouldn't?'

rows.label: Integrity
rows.value: Information has not been tampered with by unauthorised parties. Violated by: MitM attacks, SQL injection modifying records, fraudulent transactions. Ask: 'Can we trust that this hasn't been altered?'

rows.label: Availability
rows.value: Systems accessible to authorised users when needed. Violated by: ransomware, DDoS, backup destruction, infrastructure failure. Ask: 'What happens if this becomes inaccessible?'

rows.label: Vulnerability
rows.value: A weakness — an unpatched CVE, a default credential, a misconfigured permission, a human who can be manipulated. The weakness alone causes no harm.

rows.label: Exploit
rows.value: The technique that turns a vulnerability into unauthorised access. Not every vulnerability has a working exploit. A working exploit changes everything.

rows.label: Payload
rows.value: What the attacker does after getting in: ransomware, reverse shell, credential dumper, data exfiltration script. The payload delivers the actual damage.

rows.label: Script Kiddie
rows.value: Low skill, high volume. Uses pre-built tools. Motivation: curiosity/recognition. Dangerous because of scale, not sophistication.

rows.label: Hacktivist
rows.value: Ideological motivation. Targets for symbolic impact. Common: DDoS, data leaks, defacement. Examples: Anonymous.

rows.label: Cybercriminal
rows.value: Profit-motivated. Professional operations. Ransomware, financial fraud, stolen data resale. Often organised like businesses.

rows.label: Insider Threat
rows.value: Already inside the perimeter. Has access and institutional knowledge. Motivated by greed, disgruntlement, or coercion. Hardest to detect.

rows.label: Nation-State/APT
rows.value: Government-sponsored. Long-term, sophisticated, well-resourced. Goals: espionage, infrastructure disruption, economic advantage. Think SolarWinds.
